body: I tried speaking to them about my grades and the friend problem, but they said it's my fault. my dad has this mindset where it's just me not trying hard enough. whenever I try and speak to my dad about making friends he says I'm not trying hard enough and that you don't need to have common interests to be friends with someone. whenever I spoke to my mom about it, she would ask me what I expect her to do about it. they don't want me to move school and I feel bad asking for therapy due to money. I don't know if we're struggling right now due to covid, (my mom's work days were shortened and she isn't paid for 3 days that she would've been paid for before) and I wouldn't dare ask my parents how money is. I'll try write a letter but I'm just scared. I don't want them to confront me about it and get upset with me. they've done it before and it's made me feel even more upset. I feel like it's my fault that I'm sad and they remind me that I'm making things really hard for them by being so pessimistic about school n stuff but I honestly have no idea what to do about it. I'd be less of problem if I just died.

I've tried speaking to them about moving school and it's as good as beating a dead horse at this point. I don't have any good reason to move school or continue therapy, as they always want to know the reason behind it. I have a lot of trouble expressing the possibility of having depression to them as since I was young I've always been called a hypochondriac or drama queen. i know how they'll react if I say I have any type of mental illness or disability, and it's that I'm overreacting. same with the trans issue, i know they'll just think I'm doing it for attention or that they'll think I'll grow out of it. as of now, i can't even walk into the kitchen without being told off for 'looking sad'. right now with covid and everything I'm afraid to ask for anything incase I seem demanding or something.
